rationale: The hypothesis posits that microcephaly and synophrys/arched eyebrows have 100% penetrance strictly in intragenic BRD4 point mutant cohorts and drop significantly when 19p13.12 microdeletion patients are included. This is contradicted by primary records and cohort descriptions. First, OMIM entry #620568 clarifies that even among individuals harboring BRD4 point mutations, only 'some of the patients had microcephaly, arched eyebrows, synophrys', directly disproving the baseline assertion of 100% penetrance in isolated point mutant cohorts. Second, clinical characterization of 19p13.12p13.11 microdeletions encompassing BRD4 (Alesi et al., 2019) specifically highlights microcephaly, developmental delay, and synophrys as shared cardinal traits between contiguous gene deletion patients and BRD4 point mutation carriers rather than features whose frequencies attenuate upon deletion inclusion.

evidence.text: OMIM notes that among individuals evaluated with BRD4 alterations defining Cornelia de Lange syndrome 6, only some of the patients presented with microcephaly, arched eyebrows, and synophrys, contradicting the premise of uniform 100% frequency in point-mutant cohorts.

conflicts: The premise that intragenic BRD4 point mutant cohorts show 100% penetrance for microcephaly and synophrys is contradicted by OMIM #620568, which documents that only 'some' of the reported point mutant patients display these specific craniofacial features.

The assertion that microcephaly and synophrys frequencies drop when contiguous 19p13 microdeletion patients are included is contradicted by Alesi et al. (2019), who identify microcephaly and synophrys as core defining shared traits across 19p microdeletions encompassing BRD4.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerator-denominator phenotypic frequencies for microcephaly (HP:0000252) and synophrys (HP:0000664) across all published isolated single-nucleotide BRD4 variants versus multi-gene 19p13.12 microdeletions?
new_directions.rationale: Directly pooling individual patient data from all reported BRD4 single-nucleotide variant carriers and contiguous 19p13.12 microdeletion carriers would resolve whether haploinsufficiency of BRD4 alone versus flanking genes (e.g., GIPC1, NOTCH3) alters the penetrance of cardinal CdLS craniofacial traits.
